#### \*\*Similar to and answered as ‘Describe how morbid obesity might affect washout after inhalational  anaesthesia’

Morbid Obesity is defined as a BMI \>35kg/m2 

Morbid obesity results in the following changes relevant to Volatile anaesthetic washout 

- ↑Lean body mass (20% of increase)
- ↑Adipose Tissue (80% of Increase
- CVS changes: ↑Blood Volume; ↑Cardiac Output
- Respiratory changes: ↓FRV; ↑MV; ↓respiratory system compliance

Modelling of Inhalation Anaesthetic Agent compartment uptake follows a 5 compartment model: 

![](/content/exams/anzca/2015/B/5/standard-image15.png){fig-alt="Five-compartment inhalational anaesthetic model"}

V1 rapidly (minutes) equilibrates with blood but has low capacity 

V2 has moderate (hours) time to equilibration moderate capacity

V3-5 slow (days) time to equilibration but high capacity - usually minimal uptake in most anaesthesia 

**Washout**

Washout of inhalation anaesthetic agent is dependent on establishing and maintaining a decreasing concentration gradient from compartment → blood → alveolus → circuit.  

Washout is a multi-exponential process graphed by FA/FA0 curve

![](/content/exams/anzca/2015/B/5/standard-image16.png){fig-alt="Washout curves comparing normal and obese patients"}

Phases:

1.  **Rapid washout of agent from Circuit and FRC**

    - Circuit wash out dependant on FGF and circuit volume, t=CV/FGF
    - FRC washout dependant on MV and FRC volume t=FRC/MV

2.  **Washout from blood to alveolus:**

    ↑CO → lower ΔP across alveolar membrane → slower washout

    ↓Blood:gas partition coefficient →↑ agent ΔP across alveolar membrane → Rapid washout

3.  **Washout form Compartments → Blood**

    - Duration of Anaesthesia: ↑ Duration →↑uptake into body compartments → slower washout
    - Final end-tidal partial pressure of agent: ↑final concentration → increased tissue concentration → slower washout 
    - O:G partition coefficient: Highly lipid soluble agents with have will have an increased amount of drug dissolved in tissue, so a large reservoir of drug exists that will have to be removed.

**Specific Changes with Obesity:**

↑CO → slower washout 

↑ Blood Volume → Slower washout as larger V1

↓FRC → Faster washout 

↑ Compartment volumes (V2-5 compartments) → Slower washout 

↑V2 → variable result, may ↑time to awakening in short case due to redistribution but overall slower terminal elimination washout due to increased amount absorbed  

Terminal elimination additionally affected by:

↑Risk of OSA → reduced MV 

↓FRC → may be closer to closing capacity → gas trapping and sewer washout
